items.title: New school curriculum to introduce Sabah identity elements in Year One and Form One next year
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 12 — Elements reflecting Sabah’s identity will be incorporated into the new school curriculum for Year One and Form One students from the next academic session, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said. Fadhlina said Sabah Education, Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk James Ratib had given his full support to the proposal. Fadhlina said incorporating elements of Sabah’s identity into the curriculum was important in strengthening ties among Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, which she described as a foundation of Malaysia’s strength.

items.title: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles: SeoulS
items.summary: Seoul, Sept 12, 2026 (AFP) - North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles Saturday, Seoul said, a day after South Korea concluded five days of joint maritime drills with the United States and Japan that were focused on the North. Pyongyang last month slammed plans for the so-called Freedom Edge joint exercises in international waters off South Korea as a "threat" to North Korea and other countries of the region. In its last test, North Korea fired a barrage of missiles into the sea on August 20, despite an overture from US President Donald Trump, who said he planned to meet this year with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

items.title: Malaysia-Russia ties in focus as PM Anwar, Putin meet at Brics summit
items.summary: It marked Anwar’s first bilateral meeting upon his arrival here to participate in the summit in Malaysia’s capacity as a BRICS partner country since January 1, 2025. The meeting underscored the importance of maintaining high-level engagement between the two countries, particularly as Malaysia seeks to deepen economic and strategic ties with major emerging economies. Malaysia and Russia have maintained longstanding diplomatic relations since 1967, with cooperation spanning trade and investment, energy, education, tourism, defence and other areas.

items.title: Anwar welcomes Western push to ban trade with illegal Israeli settlements
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has welcomed the joint statement issued on September 8 by the foreign ministers of 12 Western countries regarding measures against illegal Israeli settlements. He said the steps represent an overdue shift in the approach of several Western governments and must now be matched by firm implementation. Anwar said he noted in particular that Britain, Canada and France would bring forward measures to ban trade in settlement goods, joining several European countries that have already taken this step.

items.title: MCMC probes claims Claude AI targeted Malaysian voters, but says issue outside its mandate
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 11 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is examining claims that Anthropic’s Claude artificial intelligence platform was used to operate a commercial election manipulation campaign targeting users in Malaysia. MCMC said it took the US AI company’s latest report seriously but stressed that the activities described fell outside its functions and mandate. “MCMC was not involved in any activities or dealings as described in the report,” it said in a statement today.

items.title: Man arrested over alleged murder of mother in Tambunan
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Police arrested a 31-year-old man on suspicion of murdering his mother at a rented house in Kampung Katagayan, Tambunan, yesterday. Keningau district police chief superintendent Erwansyah Abdul Basir said police were alerted to the incident involving the 56-year-old victim at about 2pm and subsequently tracked down the suspect. "The suspect was taken to the Tambunan police station, where he was arrested by the Criminal Investigation Department team from the Keningau district police headquarters," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Anwar to meet Modi, leading Indian companies on Brics summit sidelines today
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to have three bilateral meetings today on the sidelines of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit here. His third bilateral meeting is with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. India assumed its fourth BRICS chairship on January 1, 2026.

items.title: Magnitude 6.6 earthquake strikes Indonesia's Java region
items.summary: HAMILTON: A 6.6 magnitude earthquake struck near Teluknaga in Indonesia's Northeastern Java province on Friday, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing the US Geological Survey (USGS). The earthquake occurred at 4.23am local time (2123 GMT) on Friday at a depth of approximately 358.6km (222.8 miles). – Bernama-Anadolu © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: 'Mount Kinabalu trespassers should face jail'
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: People who violate Mount Kinabalu should be jailed to deter others from desecrating the sacred park in Kundasang, Ranau, deputy state secretary Datuk Jamili Nais said. "Climbing the sacred Mount Kinabalu without a valid permit and through an unauthorised route ought to be criminalised. Violators should spend time in jail to deter others," he said.

items.title: Stronger Asean health cooperation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia on Thursday opened the 17th Asean Health Ministers' Meeting (AHMM) and Related Meetings, with Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad chairing the gathering for the first time in 22 years under the theme "Healthy Asean: Together Towards Equitable, Future-Ready Health Systems". Dzulkefly, who chaired the meeting as Malaysia holds the Asean Health Ministers' chairmanship, with Myanmar as vice-chair, said the gathering marked a new phase in regional health cooperation, focusing on translating policy into action for Asean's 670 million people. The five-day conference, which began on Monday and ended yesterday, brought together health ministers and senior health officials from Asean member states, along with dialogue partners, World Health Organisation (WHO) representatives and technical experts.

items.title: 30 bodies recovered from burned ferry, 54 still missing off western Philippines
items.summary: MANILA: The Philippine Coast Guard said Friday that 30 bodies had been recovered from the charred remains of a passenger ferry that caught fire off the western Philippine province of Palawan earlier this week, while 54 people remained missing, Anadolu Ajansi reported. The MV June Aster was initially reported to be carrying 117 passengers and 17 crew members when it departed Manila for Coron in Palawan before catching fire Wednesday night. Five people were confirmed dead that same night, while 43 passengers and crew members were rescued.

items.title: Nod for Kolej Poly-Tech Mara's Diploma in Accounting
items.summary: BANGI: The recognition of Kolej Poly-Tech Mara Sdn Bhd's (KPTMSB) Diploma in Accounting (AA101) by the Malaysian Institute of Certified Public Accountants (MICPA) will strengthen pathways towards professional accounting qualifications. KPTMSB chief executive officer Radzuan Razali said the recognition reflected the programme's alignment with academic and professional standards set by MICPA. He said it would expose students to professional accounting standards, practices and expectations beyond the lecture hall.

items.title: US judge blocks Trump administration's 'loyalty' question for job applicants
items.summary: BOSTON, (United States): A federal judge on Friday blocked US President Donald Trump's administration from continuing to ask applicants for civil service jobs throughout the government to respond to what unions described as a partisan "loyalty question." US District Judge George O'Toole in Boston sided with three unions representing government workers who sued last year after the administration began asking applicants for nonpartisan federal jobs to write essays explaining how they would help advance Trump's policies and executive orders. The unions, including the American Federation of Government Employees, argued the question mandated by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) unlawfully politicized the hiring process for career government workers by attempting to assess their support for the Republican president.

items.title: High-profile cases keep courts busy this week
items.summary: The courts were abuzz with a teenage murder trial, Interpol's assistance sought to locate former research officer Yusoff Rawther, former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim's court appearance, three more alleged gang members being charged with murder and a corporate chief executive claiming trial to cheating charges. Below are the other big cases this week: THE Bandar Utama school murder trial entered its final stretch, with the prosecution and defence completing their oral clarification before Shah Alam High Court judge Adlin Abdul Majid. ON Thursday, Alam Maritim Resources Bhd group managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Azmi Ahmad, 67, claimed trial to two cheating charges involving shipping daily charter rates.

items.title: Saudi says drones launched from Iraq hit oil pipeline
items.summary: RIYADH: Saudi Arabia on Friday said drones launched from Iraq hit the East-West pipeline and led to its closure. The foreign ministry condemned "the targeting of the East-West pipeline in the Riyadh and Medina regions by several drones coming from Iraq, which caused human injuries and damage". Saudi Arabia says the attacks that occurred on Thursday morning had left several people wounded.

items.title: Drug lab, slain syndicate chief, airport security gaps and Nibong Tebal abduction among major crimes this week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have shut down a large-scale drug processing laboratory hidden inside an industrial premises in Selangor, seizing more than 13 tonnes of liquid and powdered MDMA and other drugs estimated to be worth RM2.4 billion in Op Eumenes. The operation followed intelligence and surveillance on the syndicate, with six simultaneous and follow-up raids conducted in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur where it saw five suspects aged 29 to 43 arrested. Police also seized five vehicles and other assets worth RM276,000 under the Dangerous Drugs (Forfeiture of Property) Act 1988.

items.title: Anwar, Putin move to fast-track bilateral deals, improve direct air connectivity
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Russian President Vladimir Putin have agreed to fast-track the implementation of bilateral agreements while pushing ahead with measures to strengthen air connectivity between the two countries. The two leaders also discussed expediting direct air connectivity between Malaysia and Russia, alongside visa-free travel, which could facilitate greater movement of tourists, business travellers and investors between the two markets. Anwar also raised the prospect of increased Russian imports of Malaysian palm oil, potentially opening wider market access for Malaysian producers and strengthening agricultural trade between the two countries.

items.title: Umno, Pas tie-up a win-win for both parties, say analysts [WATCH]
items.summary: Dr Lau Zhe Wei said BN would have better prospects of winning more seats and securing the top leadership position through cooperation with Pas. "If BN were to work with Pas, the outcome would likely be better for them compared with working with PH." Lau said the current political landscape and the strength of Malay unity sentiments made Pas a more suitable partner for BN than PH.

items.title: Ebola infections top 7,000 in Congo as virus spreads to new province
items.summary: DAKAR: The number of confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo has passed 7,000, with the virus spreading to a new province, government data showed on Friday. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, became the largest and deadliest in Congo's history after surpassing the 2018–2020 epidemic. Government figures showed late on Friday that the death toll had risen to 3,398, while confirmed cases reached 7,022 across seven provinces.

items.title: Train derails in northwest France, 44 injured
items.summary: PARIS: A train carrying 186 passengers derailed in northwest France on Friday, injuring 44 people, one of them seriously, officials said. The train was running between the Normandy cities of Rouen and Caen, Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said on X. It derailed around 7.45pm (1745 GMT), local authorities said in a statement, and a mass-casualty response plan had been activated, with 130 firefighters, five medical teams and 80 vehicles deployed.

items.title: North Korea launches unidentified projectile, South Korea says
items.summary: SEOUL: North Korea launched an unidentified projectile toward the sea to the east of the Korean Peninsula, South Korea's defence ministry said on Saturday. South Korea's Yonhap news agency reported earlier that South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff are analysing the projectile's specifications and range. Last month, North Korea launched more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles and ordered its military to maintain full readiness during South Korea's ongoing joint exercises with the US.

items.title: Iran says to discuss Hormuz with Gulf states in Oman on Monday
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's foreign ministry said the country would meet with Gulf states in Oman on Monday to discuss the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which the Islamic republic has blockaded during the Middle East war. Iran has been at war since February 28, when US-Israeli strikes killed its supreme leader. Iran retaliated with attacks across the region and blockaded the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of world oil supplies previously flowed.

items.title: Remember the 5 heroes who delivered hope to interior Sarawak
items.summary: AS we celebrate Malaysia Day next week, we are reminded that sometimes, it takes a tragedy to pull us together as Malaysians. When a friend related earlier this week how he cried over an amateur video of an apparently stricken helicopter on a Flying Doctor Service run deep in Sarawak's interior before it hit the ground and was incinerated, I knew this incident will cut deeply. Five Malaysian heroes, all in their prime, paid with their own lives while extending otherwise hard-to-access, life-saving medical services to isolated native communities in Borneo's jungle-clad highlands.

items.title: NST Leader: Finally, AI governance
items.summary: MALAYSIA'S first ever dedicated horizontal legal framework on artificial intelligence (AI) governance is ready to be tabled in Parliament in Q1 2027. All must welcome the Bill. AI is already being used in business, education, healthcare, finance, government and everyday life.

items.title: 'That's why we fight': Trump links 9/11 to Iran conflict
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump vowed Friday that the United States would never forget the Sept 11, 2001 attacks and suggested the country was continuing the "war on terror" 25 years later by fighting Iran. Speaking at the Pentagon after skipping the main 9/11 commemorations in New York, Republican Trump also hit out at domestic "fanatics" in an apparent swipe at Democrats. That's why we fight today," Trump said in a speech.

items.title: China's robot champion races towards real-world work
items.summary: A WEEK after his robot outran humanity's fastest man, Jack Guo is already chasing a harder goal. TianGong Ultra stunned spectators at the World Humanoid Robot Games when it covered 100m in 8.64 seconds, almost a full second faster than Usain Bolt's world record. "When it started smoothly and got past 50m, that was when I finally relaxed," said Guo, who leads the development of Ultra and Omni — a smaller model used in 400m races — at the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Centre, known as X-Humanoid.

items.title: Hong Kong sentences Tiananmen activists to between 5 and 7 years in jail
items.summary: HONG KONG: A Hong Kong court handed three Tiananmen vigil activists jail sentences of between five and seven years on Friday for national security crimes, drawing international condemnation. The United Nations, rights groups and foreign governments have condemned the sentences, issued under a national security law that Beijing imposed on Hong Kong in 2020 following huge pro-democracy protests. Lee and Chow, who pleaded not guilty, were sentenced to seven years and seven years and three months, respectively, AFP journalists in court heard.

items.title: Scammers forge KL DoE documents to cheat suppliers out of RM200,000
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Kuala Lumpur Department of Environment (DoE) has detected eight government procurement order scams abusing its name, resulting in losses exceeding RM200,000 for two suppliers. Director Sharifah Zakiah Syed Sahab said the department first detected the scam on Sept 4, when a representative from a diving equipment supplier visited to verify government procurement documents. "Before that, the department received several inquiries regarding procurement documents starting in mid-August.

items.title: Health Ministry urged to strengthen transport safety after helicopter crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Joint Council of Presidents and Secretaries-General of the Health Ministry Workers Union (Mapsu) has urged the Health Ministry to strengthen safety standards for air, sea and river transport used in healthcare services following the recent Long Lellang helicopter crash in Sarawak. Mapsu president Ajulahin Japin said the safety of healthcare workers must be given serious and preventive attention. He said the ministry must not focus solely on aviation safety, but also ensure that water transport complies with strict safety standards.

items.title: Sabah and Sarawak challenges must be part of national journey, says PKR Youth chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The history and challenges faced by Sabah and Sarawak must be viewed as part of Malaysia's collective experience to elevate the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) into a national narrative. PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim said a true national narrative goes beyond asking Peninsular Malaysians to understand the demands of the two Borneo states. "The history of Sabah and Sarawak is our history.

items.title: Cameron Highlands hit by landslide and flash floods after heavy rain [WATCH]
items.summary: The incident, reported at 4.50pm, prompted the closure to ensure public safety and facilitate earth-clearing works by the Public Works Department (PWD) and YP Maintenance. District police chief Superintendent Azri Ramli said authorities were closely monitoring the clearing works and would reopen the road once it was deemed safe. The public is advised to avoid the road temporarily," he said in a statement.

items.title: Anwar takes subtle jab at Zahid with 'Guru', 'slay' references
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has taken a subtle jab at his deputy, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, echoing the "Guru" and "slay" references used by the Umno president in recent remarks. Anwar used both terms while updating Malaysians on his diplomatic mission to India. Zahid's use of "Guru", or teacher, echoed a leaked telephone conversation between Zahid and Anwar in April 2021, during which Zahid referred to Anwar as "Guru."

items.title: Super El Nino could bring 40°C temperatures to Malaysia by early 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia faces an extreme heatwave with temperatures potentially reaching 40 degrees Celsius between January and May next year due to an impending Super El Nino phenomenon. MetMalaysia said that historical meteorological records associate strong El Nino episodes with elevated temperatures, dry conditions, and severe haze risks. Previous Super El Nino events in 1997/1998 and 2015/2016 recorded daily maximum temperatures far more extreme than usual.

items.title: Lorry driver who crashed into Kajang eatery fell asleep, say police
items.summary: KAJANG: A lorry driver whose vehicle crashed into the front of an eatery in Jalan Batu 12, Cheras, yesterday was believed to have fallen asleep at the wheel, and was not driving under the influence of alcohol as alleged online. Kajang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said the incident occurred at 6.30pm as the lorry was heading towards Cheras. "No casualties or injuries were reported," Naazron said in a statement today.

items.title: Body of unidentified man found along Sungai Langat
items.summary: District police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said police received a report on the discovery at 6pm and dispatched a team to the scene. He said initial checks found the body on the riverbank, before Fire and Rescue Department personnel helped retrieve it. "Preliminary checks by the Forensic Unit found no visible injuries on the body to suggest foul play.

items.title: KL DOE warns of fake procurement scams after two suppliers lose more than RM200,000
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — The Kuala Lumpur Department of Environment (DOE) has detected several attempts by irresponsible parties to commit fraud using the department’s name. She said her department first detected the scam on September 4, when a representative of a diving equipment supplier came to the department to verify the authenticity of government procurement documents. “Prior to that, KL DOE also received several inquiries regarding these government procurement documents starting in mid-August, and last Tuesday (September 8) from a supplier company representative who also came to inquire about a souvenir order worth more than RM100,000 supposedly made by KL DOE for an upcoming programme,” she told Bernama, here today.

items.title: Fire Dept: Two men found dead in separate incidents in Penang drain and Perak river
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 11 — Two men were found dead in separate incidents in Penang and Perak today, one in a drain near a school here and the other in Sungai Perak. The body of Ooi Chai Siang, 37, was found in a drain about 1.5 metres deep near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Tun Hussein Onn in Taman Kelisa Emas here today. Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said the department received a call from the police at 12.10pm requesting assistance to retrieve the body.

items.title: PM Anwar heads to India for BRICS summit, bilateral talks with world leaders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — After concluding his working visit to Sabah today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim departed for New Delhi to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit, where he is also scheduled to hold several bilateral meetings. In a Facebook post, Anwar said he was scheduled to meet the Prime Minister of India, as well as the presidents of Russia, Iran and Kazakhstan and the Prime Minister of Ethiopia. “My delegation and I have departed for New Delhi, India to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit.

items.title: Past is past, but Umno delegates want PAS to prove it can be different
items.summary: At 68, the Umno Kuala Krai division secretary has seen the party’s relationship with PAS shift from cooperation to rivalry and back again. Muhammad said any renewed cooperation between Umno and PAS would require both sides to make compromises, particularly over the allocation of seats in the next election. PAS members attend the Umno Youth General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur yesterday.

items.title: Economy minister: Sabah receives RM582m, highest allocation for small-scale projects nationwide since 2023
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — A total of RM1.52 billion has been allocated for 8,069 small-scale projects and People’s Facility Initiatives (IKR) nationwide since 2023, with Sabah receiving the largest share at RM582.29 million for 2,301 projects. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said RM175.24 million of the allocation for Sabah was channelled for the implementation of 985 IKR projects, and RM407.05 million was for 1,316 small-scale projects. For this year alone, he said, Sabah received RM113.3 million to implement 481 IKR and small-scale projects, out of a total national allocation of RM323.8 million.

items.title: GISBH fails in bid to challenge Kedah fatwa declaring teachings deviant
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 11 — The Alor Setar High Court has dismissed an application by GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH) and its Chief Executive Officer, Nasiruddin Mohd Ali, for leave to initiate judicial review proceedings to challenge a state fatwa issued against them last year. The fatwa, issued by the Kedah State Fatwa Committee on February 12 last year, ruled that the beliefs, teachings, tenets and practices of GISBH members and followers were deviant and contrary to Islamic teachings. The applicants named the Kedah State Fatwa Committee, Kedah State Islamic Religious Council and Mufti of Kedah as respondents.

items.title: Penang LRT works to close part of Jalan Magazine for 21 days from Sept 14
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 11 — Jalan Magazine here will be closed for 21 days from September 14 to facilitate road widening and utility relocation works for the LRT Mutiara Line project. “The closure will involve the leftmost lane of Jalan Magazine in front of St. Giles Wembley Hotel heading towards KOMTAR, while the other lanes will remain open to traffic,” it said in a statement today. It said a partial lane closure would also be implemented intermittently along Jalan Sultan Azlan Shah from 8am to 4pm daily from September 16 to December 15 to facilitate construction of the LRT Mutiara Line, including drainage and road widening works.

items.title: Malaysians scamming Malaysians: Indonesia nab 30 in Pontianak hotel raid
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 11 — Indonesian authorities have detained 30 Malaysians suspected of running online scam activities from a hotel in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, allegedly targeting fellow Malaysians. Pontianak Immigration Office chief Sam Fernando said the Malaysians, comprising 22 men and eight women, were detained along with a Taiwanese man at the hotel at about 11.15am on Tuesday in a joint operation with Pontianak City Police following intelligence on suspicious activities involving foreigners. Sam said the 31 foreign nationals had used 14 rooms in the hotel for their activities.

items.title: Chief minister says Melaka election not far off, dissolution of DUN required by year‑end
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, September 11 — As talks and speculation on the upcoming Melaka state election intensify, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has hinted that the wait will be neither too long nor too soon. Speaking to the press during the 2026 Umno General Assembly at World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL), Rauf said that that Melaka must dissolve its state legislative assembly (DUN) by the end of December as its five year term is nearing completion. “We can’t delay the dissolution of the DUN because the date is inching closer,” Rauf said.

items.title: DNA results for five Long Lellang crash victims due by tomorrow, say Sarawak police
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 11 — The deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) analysis for all five victims of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang last Tuesday is expected to be completed by tomorrow at the latest. “We anticipate that the DNA analysis for the five victims could be completed by tomorrow at the latest,” he told reporters here today. Last Tuesday, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport.

items.title: Newborn’s body found in Dungun hostel locker, police investigating
items.summary: DUNGUN, Sept 11 — A 19-year-old student allegedly hid her newborn baby’s body in a hostel locker after giving birth in a toilet at an educational institution here two days ago. Dungun district police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said police received a report on the discovery of the body at 10.48pm yesterday. Investigations found that the student allegedly wrapped the baby in cloth, placed the body in a bag, and kept it in a hostel locker.

items.title: Tanker driver, still hospitalised, charged with murder over Pahang crash that wiped out young family on Merdeka Day
items.summary: TEMERLOH, Sept 11 — A cement tanker driver receiving treatment at Hospital Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah was charged today with four counts of murder over a crash that killed four people on Aug 31. Zulkarnain is accused of having caused the deaths of Muhammad Nazatullah Nazmi, Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan, Muhammad Armaan Nazeef Muhammad Nazatullah and Seow Beng Wai. He said Seow’s son, Sebastian Seow Jhen, 18, who was driving the Honda CR-V, and the tanker driver sustained serious injuries and were treated at Hospital Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah in Temerloh.

items.title: Selangor sets Oct 26 as replacement holiday for Sultan’s Silver Jubilee
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 11 — Selangor has declared October 25 a special public holiday to commemorate the silver jubilee of Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah’s reign. State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin said the holiday would be replaced on October 26 as the anniversary falls on a Sunday, The Star reported. He added that the holiday would be observed in the same way as the September 1 public holiday marking Selangor’s overall victory at Sukma 2026.

items.title: Was bad weather to blame? Investigators dig into what brought down deadly Long Lellang chopper
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau has begun its investigation into the cause of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang which claimed five lives, said Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah. Hasbi said the ministry’s air accident investigation team was already at the crash site and was working to determine the cause of the tragedy. “We will wait for the report from the Air Accident Investigation Team.

items.title: PM Anwar visits Kampung Numbak fire victims, pledges aid
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim visited and offered support to victims of the Kampung Numbak fire at the temporary relief centre at the Damai Multipurpose Hall here today. Anwar, accompanied by Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor, arrived at the relief centre at 1.30 pm and spent about 20 minutes meeting the victims. The Prime Minister was then briefed on the fire by Kota Kinabalu Mayor Datuk Seri Dr Sabin Samitah before handing over aid to the victims.

items.title: Zahid: Umno proposing ‘Grand Collaboration’ to end political clashes in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — A proposal for the formation of a “Grand Collaboration” through political understanding (Tafahum Siyasi) among the country’s political party coalitions has been put forward to avoid political clashes that would be detrimental to the ummah and the nation, said Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said the concept does not involve a merger of political parties, but rather a common ground for mutual understanding aimed at preserving political stability and reinvigorating national economic growth. In other words, whoever Umno and Barisan Nasional (BN) work with, Umno remains Umno, and Barisan Nasional remains Barisan Nasional,” he said.

items.title: Sabah gets RM1.5b MA63 boost, Anwar hints Sarawak could be next by Sept 16
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — The interim allocation for Sabah will immediately rise to RM1.5 billion this year, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said this in reply to a request from Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Panglima Hajiji Noor during the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Council meeting (MTPMA63) press conference here. That is on behalf of the Sabah government,” said Hajiji.

items.title: From complaint to compensation: How victims in Malaysia are winning sexual harassment cases
items.summary: SEMPORNA, Sept 11 — The Sexual Harassment Tribunal Agency (Tags) under the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) recorded 134 sexual harassment complaints over a two-year period, with 90 of them successfully resolved. Male victims and children can also use this platform to seek redress. “Some victims have also won their cases and received compensation,” she told reporters after officiating the Semporna Zero Tolerance for Violence: Advocacy Against Sexual Harassment and End Violence Against Women programmes here yesterday.

items.title: DNA tests pending for five victims of Long Lellang helicopter crash, says Sarawak police
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 11 — The post-mortems on all five victims of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang last Tuesday were completed at 7.30pm yesterday. Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said the cause of death for all five victims was severe burn injuries sustained in the helicopter crash. On Tuesday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia said a BO-105 helicopter carrying five individuals, including the pilot, had crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport.

items.title: Perak orders caterer at Lenggong boarding school to shut after almost 160 students, staff fall sick
items.summary: IPOH, September 11 — A food caterer serving a boarding school in Lenggong, Perak has been ordered to close after 159 students and staff developed symptoms of suspected food poisoning. Perak Health, Human Resources, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said the Hulu Perak District Health Office received a report of the incident from Lenggong Health Clinic on September 10. Sivanesan also urged food handlers to comply with the Food Act 1983 and Food Hygiene Regulations 2009 to prevent further food poisoning incidents.

items.title: No U-turn: Ex-minister Dr Zaliha says she has backed Health Service Commission proposal since 2023
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Former Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa today denied making a U-turn on the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission, saying she had remained committed to the initiative since 2023. In a statement, Dr Zaliha said that as early as February 2023, she had publicly stated that the proposal to establish the commission was among the key matters being considered in the final draft of the Health White Paper. “In fact, in April 2023, the same news portal reported on my meeting with representatives of Hartal Doktor Kontrak (HDK), where the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission and a Health Reform Commission was discussed within the framework of the White Paper,” she said.

items.title: Anwar: Time to make MA63 part of the national conversation, not just Sabah-Sarawak issue
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) to become part of the national narrative rather than being viewed solely as an issue concerning Sabah and Sarawak. He said the approach was important to ensure Malaysians understood that the government’s commitment to MA63 formed part of the Madani Government’s national policy and was closely linked to the country’s development, stability and unity. Anwar said this must be understood and embraced by people in peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak as part of a national policy, commitment and narrative aimed at strengthening the country.

items.title: Sounds like a ‘PM in waiting’, Khairy says of Zahid’s speech at Umno assembly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s keynote at the party’s general assembly this morning earned praise from Khairy Jamaluddin. Khairy, an Umno returnee after being sacked three years ago for alleged disciplinary infractions and breaches of party discipline during GE15 – described the speech as crystal clear on Barisan Nasional’s (BN) direction ahead of the coming general election. “This is the speech of a prime minister in waiting and a speech of a government in waiting,” Khairy told reporters after Zahid’s speech at the 2026 Umno general assembly here.

items.title: Sabah, Sarawak to get bigger share of Parliament seats, Anwar says as MA63 push moves ahead
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Sabah and Sarawak will get a higher proportion of parliamentary representation under a Cabinet decision in principle to increase the number of seats for the two Borneo states, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today. Anwar said the Cabinet had agreed to increase the number of parliamentary seats for Sabah and Sarawak, although the exact number and mechanism had yet to be determined. Anwar added that there could also be an increase in seats for peninsular Malaysia.

items.title: Zahid says Umno still hopes for favourable outcome after Najib clemency deferred
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today expressed disappointment over the postponement of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency application, but said the party continues to hope for a favourable outcome. Zahid said Umno respected the decision and would continue to uphold the institution of the Malay Rulers while appealing to His Majesty the King to use his wisdom in deciding Najib’s application. The Prime Minister’s Department today said Najib’s clemency application had been deferred to a future sitting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board.
